correctness.rationale: For p∤n, multiply floor by p², invert p² modulo n, and reduce the gcd to the residue t_r. For n=pm, exact gcd equals m gcd(p,a p^(k-2)m^(k-1)), giving unique exception k=2,n=p. Upper period p²Q drops to pQ for p|k by binomial lifting. Any eventual period must contain p by a unit-vs-multiple-of-p CRT witness and each prime ℓ|Q by a second CRT witness. If p∤k, translation by p times a unit cycles all p lifts of each nonzero residue and would force equal radical supports; lifts contain coprime u,u+p, contradiction. CRT gives density. All boundary cases including p=2 and k=2 were checked. Exact rational code passed 693 parameter sets and 95 complete periods; proof supplies infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The natural recent problem asks for coprimality of n with a rational floor polynomial. The minimal eventual period is a meaningful arithmetic invariant not implied by a general periodicity upper bound: it exhibits an exact prime-adic phase transition when p divides k. The unique preperiod exception in the quadratic family sharply distinguishes eventual from full periodicity. The theorem covers every prime and all exponents at the first nontrivial prime-power denominator, and supplies density, useful for subsequent prime-power analysis; it is not an isolated numerical computation.
